c74object.name: evi_baxandall
c74object.digest: evieve Gen Object. Emulation of a classic baxandall EQ
c74object.description:
evi_baxandall is an abstraction for using inside gen~ or GenExpr.
evi_baxandall.gendsp requires the GenExpr file(s):
evi_smooth.genexpr
evi_baxandall is also available in MSP as: evi.baxandall~.
An EQ tone control shape popularised in the 1950s, often used in HiFi equipment and guitar amplifiers. Baxandall is a special EQ as the frequency response is fixed, and depends on the simple high level gain control inputs ('treble' and 'bass').

geninlet.name: mono
geninlet.digest: / Left. Mono or left input depending on @stereo attribute.

geninlet.name: none
geninlet.digest: / Right. Nothing or right input depending on @stereo attribute.

attribute.name: bass
attribute.description: The amount of bass in the tone. As a baxandall EQ, this also shapes the frequency response, creating a mid frequency notch at high levels. Ultimately 'bass' and 'treble' behave like shelving filters, at opposite extremes creating a tilt-like filter.

attribute.name: smooth
attribute.description: If on, the internal coefficients are lightly smoothed at an optimal part in the DSP chain. If not updating 'treble' and 'bass' dynamically 'smooth' can safely be turned off.

attribute.name: stereo
attribute.description: If @stereo is on, the EQ is stereo input stereo output. If @stereo is off, the EQ is mono in mono out (left in and out).

attribute.name: treble
attribute.description: The amount of treble in the tone. As a baxandall EQ, this also shapes the frequency response, creating a high mid frequency notch at high levels. Ultimately 'bass' and 'treble' behave like shelving filters, at opposite extremes creating a tilt-like filter.
